description: Somos 4 estudiantes de Ingeniería Electromecánica del TEC apasionados por resolver problemas de ingeniería y datos. Nuestra experiencia combina hardware, sistemas eléctricos, análisis térmico/fluidos, modelado de datos e integración de software inteligente. Buscamos complementar el equipo con personas en Desarrollo Web, Visualización de Datos, codificación y otras áreas.
summary: This project presents the design and development of an educational video game focused on strategic resource management and life support within a lunar outpost. The premise challenges the player to ensure the survival of an astronaut through the repurposing and transformation of materials and components from their own spacecraft. The simulation integrates scientific models grounded in NASA technical guidelines, incorporating critical variables such as space radiation levels, crew metabolic expenditure, oxygen and water recovery and purification, and the impact of thermal and illumination cycles derived from lunar rotation. Furthermore, the system implements agricultural and nutritional bioregeneration modules, including hydroponic crops grown from non-hybrid seeds and cricket rearing as a sustainable protein source. Targeted at high school and university students, as well as anyone interested in astronautics, the game serves as a rigorous, interactive pedagogical tool designed to convey the physiological risks, operational logistics, and engineering challenges involved in sustaining human life on the Moon.
details: This proyect was created on Visual Studio Code using Vite and TypeScript as it was intended as aweboage, it was hosted in Vercel, an open source hosting tool and Phaser used for helping the animations. Our project is focused on the education of resource management in the moon, the game helps students to understand how it would be to create a moon base on a pixel art style game. Based on real data, we managed to create a realistic simulation of survival in this space environment, providing a thrilling adventure for young curious minds.
